Need to search first.I couldn't write the commentary notes. The research tools hit their usage limit before I had read a single page.

My first round of page fetches failed because the tool only accepts links that have already turned up in a search. My next batch of ten searches then hit the server's limit. Only one search worked, and it returned page titles and links but none of the page text. Every later fetch or search was refused. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read no pages, I have no verse notes, no Protestant differences and no other views to give you.

**Useful pages that search found (none of them read yet):**
- Enduring Word (Guzik), Proverbs 11, verse by verse: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/proverbs-11/
- Enduring Word, a second Proverbs 11 page: https://enduringword.com/proverbs-11-gods-wisdom-for-justice-integrity-and-blessing/
- Guzik's Study Guide for Proverbs 11 on Blue Letter Bible: https://www.blueletterbible.org/comm/guzik_david/study-guide/proverbs/proverbs-11.cfm
- Matthew Henry, Proverbs 11 on Blue Letter Bible: https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Pro/Pro_011.cfm
- Ironside's Notes, Proverbs 11 on StudyLight: https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/isn/proverbs-11.html
- Everett's Study Notes, Proverbs 11 on StudyLight: https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghe/proverbs-11.html
- Enduring Word, Leviticus 19 (may cover honest weights, a background for v. 1): https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/leviticus-19/

**What I would do next, once the tools work again:**
1. Read the pages above, plus Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on StudyLight or BibleHub, Precept Austin, and the NET Bible notes for Proverbs 11.
2. Run targeted searches on the verses most likely to show real differences:
   - **v. 1 and v. 20:** what "abomination" means.
   - **v. 4:** "righteousness delivers from death" (Reformed, Lutheran, Wesleyan and Catholic views on righteousness).
   - **v. 15:** guaranteeing someone else's debt.
   - **vv. 24–25 and v. 28:** generosity and wealth, including how prosperity teaching is described.
   - **v. 30:** "he who wins souls" (evangelistic reading versus scholarly notes on the Hebrew).
   - **v. 31:** compared with the quotation in 1 Peter 4:18.

If you'd like, start a new session (or try again later) and I'll do the full research, with a URL for every point.
